newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate remains weak in flush market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate remains weak in flush market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 5.50/60 percent on Wednesday as the market remained highly liquid, dealers said.
They said lending by foreign banks also continued to pressure rates.
"Foreigners are still long and this will continue to keep rates under pressure," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.

Trading, however, was cautious with players closely watching movements in the Thai baht, dealers said. The baht fell sharply on Wednesday after the Bank of Thailand announced it would let the currency float.
"Players don't want to be caught again," the dealer said.

The baht came under severe attack by speculators in May which spilled over to other regional currencies. A massive intervention by Bank Negara then to support the ringgit caused a sudden tightness in the market and pushed interbank rates to unusually high levels.
Earlier, one-week money was at 6.30/35 percent against 6.30/80 on Tuesday.
One-month money was at 7.25/30 percent from 7.35/40, and three-month at 7.40/45 percent against 7.45/50.
Dealers said an outflow of 500 millon ringgit on Wednesday, due to payment for Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit against a maturity of 500 million, had no impact on rates.
Another 500-million ringgit bill issue will mature on Friday.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mostly unchanged due to uncertainty over the direction of interbank rates, futures dealers said.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was steady at 92.68, or an implied yield of 7.32 percent.
The December contract was also unchanged at 92.78, or 7.22 percent while March 1998 was down three points to 92.77, or 7.23 percent.
